name: Iceland
description: Iceland offers a unique experience for expats, known for its unparalleled natural beauty, high quality of life, and extremely low crime rates. It's a land of striking contrasts, from vibrant city life in Reykjavik to serene, wild landscapes, appealing to those seeking a strong social safety net and a close-knit community.
longdescription: Living in Iceland as an expat means immersing oneself in a country consistently ranked among the safest and happiest globally. The culture is deeply rooted in Norse mythology and Icelandic folklore, with a strong emphasis on family, work-life balance, and gender equality. Despite its small population, Iceland boasts a dynamic job market, particularly in sectors like tourism, fisheries, energy, and a growing tech industry. The economy is robust, supported by its commitment to renewable energy and a well-developed welfare system that provides affordable healthcare and education. While the cost of living, especially in Reykjavik, is high, the average monthly salary after tax allows for a comfortable lifestyle. Expats will find a clean environment and a strong sense of community, although integrating into established social circles and mastering the Icelandic language can take time.

visas.name: Long-Term Visa for Remote Workers
visas.description: This visa, officially known as a 'Long-Term Visa for Remote Workers,' allows eligible non-EEA/EFTA nationals to reside in Iceland for a temporary period while working remotely for an employer or clients based outside of Iceland. It offers an opportunity to experience life in Iceland without entering the local labor market.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a non-EEA/EFTA national who is a high-earning remote worker, freelancer, or self-employed individual earning income from abroad, seeking a temporary stay in Iceland.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa is a temporary, non-renewable stay and does not directly lead to permanent residency or citizenship in Iceland. It cannot be converted into a different residence permit while in Iceland.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa is generally not renewable; applicants must typically leave Iceland and reapply from abroad after a 12-month period since their last digital nomad visa stay.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of this visa are unlikely to be considered tax residents in Iceland, as the maximum stay is 180 days. Income tax obligations typically remain in the applicant's country of permanent residence, as worldwide income would only be subject to Icelandic tax if the stay exceeds 183 days.
benefits: Ability to live in Iceland for up to 180 days while working remotely for a foreign employer/clients.
Travel freely within the Schengen Area during the visa's validity.
Opportunity to experience daily life in Iceland beyond a short tourist stay.
Allows eligible family members (spouse/partner and dependent children) to accompany the main applicant.
required_documents: Completed Long-Term Visa application form
Valid passport (issued within the last 10 years, valid at least 3 months beyond intended stay)
One passport-sized (3.5cm x 4.5cm) photograph, taken within the last 6 months
Proof of a valid health insurance policy covering the stay in Iceland and Schengen area (minimum coverage of ISK 2,000,000)
Documents confirming purpose of stay (e.g., letter from overseas employer authorizing remote work, confirmation of self-employment)
Proof of income (e.g., employment contract, payslips, tax statements, bank statements showing salary credits, business financial records for self-employed)
Proof of accommodation in Iceland
application_process_steps: Check eligibility criteria (non-EEA/EFTA national, remote work for foreign entity, meet income).
Gather all required documents.
Pay the non-refundable application fee (12,200 ISK) by bank transfer before submission.
Complete and sign the official Long-Term Visa application form.
Submit the completed application form and all supporting documents by mail or dropbox to the Directorate of Immigration in Kópavogur, Iceland.
Wait for the application to be processed and a decision to be made by immigration authorities.

visas.name: Residence Permit for Students
visas.description: This permit is for non-EEA/EFTA citizens who intend to pursue full-time studies in Iceland for more than 90 days. It allows temporary residency for the duration of studies, with possibilities for renewal, part-time work, and family reunification under specific conditions.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EEA/EFTA citizens admitted to a recognized full-time study program at an Icelandic university, including undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, exchange, and certain technical or internship programs.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The student residence permit alone cannot be the direct basis for permanent residency. To qualify for a permanent residence permit, an applicant must have held a permit that may be the basis for permanent residency (e.g., a work permit for specialists) for at least two years, in addition to having previously held a student residence permit for at least two years, totaling at least four years of legal residence. Additionally, the applicant must not have resided abroad for more than 90 days in total each year during this period.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must remain enrolled in full-time studies (30 ECTS per semester), show satisfactory academic performance, and apply for renewal at least four weeks before the current permit expires. Financial requirements and health insurance conditions must still be met.
benefits: Legal residency in Iceland for the duration of studies.
Ability to work up to 22.5 hours per week (60%) during academic terms and full-time during official study breaks, after obtaining a separate work permit.
Possibility for family reunification for spouses/cohabiting partners, children under 18, and parents aged 67 or older (with conditions for undergraduate students).
Path to a job-seeking permit after graduation and conditional path to permanent residency.
Travel within the Schengen Area for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
required_documents: Completed and signed application form (D-108).
Payment receipt for processing fee.
One passport-sized photograph (35x45mm).
Copy of passport (personal information, signature page, and visa/stamps; valid at least 90 days beyond permit validity).
Copy of criminal record certificate (not older than 12 months).
Health insurance confirmation (valid for at least six months in Iceland, minimum coverage ISK 2,000,000).
Documents on secure means of financial support (bank statements showing required monthly amount for the permit's duration).
Confirmation of admission to a full-time study program from an Icelandic educational institution.
Proof of accommodation (rental agreement or housing confirmation - to be submitted upon arrival if not known at application time).
Application for an appropriate work permit and employment contract if applicable (for internships where work is part of studies).
application_process_steps: Gain admission to a recognized full-time study program in Iceland.
Gather all required supporting documents, ensuring they meet the Directorate's specifications.
Fill out the application form (D-108) on a computer, print, and sign it.
Pay the processing fee (70,000 ISK) by bank transfer and obtain a payment receipt.
Send the completed application form, payment receipt, and all supporting documents by mail or deliver to the drop box at the Directorate of Immigration.

Wait for the application to be processed and a decision to be communicated. Upon approval, book an appointment for a photograph for the residence permit card and undergo a medical examination if required by nationality.

visas.name: Residence Permit for Family Reunification (Parents over 67)
visas.description: This residence permit is for individuals aged 67 years or older who wish to reunite with their adult child residing in Iceland.
visas.target_applicant: An individual aged 67 or older whose adult child lives in Iceland, is an Icelandic citizen, or holds a permanent residence permit or certain temporary residence permits, and upon whom the parent is financially dependent.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This permit may form the basis for a permanent residence permit. Conditions for permanent residency typically include four years of continuous legal residence, demonstrating Icelandic language proficiency, financial self-sufficiency, and a clean criminal record, and not having resided abroad for more than 90 days in total each year.
visas.renewal_conditions: The applicant must continue to meet all original requirements. The permit may be revoked if the holder stays abroad for more than three consecutive months. Renewals are granted for a maximum of two years at a time.
benefits: Allows legal residence in Iceland.
Can serve as a basis for applying for a permanent residence permit.
Provides the possibility to apply for a separate work permit to be employed in Iceland.
required_documents: Passport photograph (35 mm x 45 mm)
Photocopy of passport (personal information page and signature page), valid at least 90 days beyond the permit's validity
Copy of a foreign criminal record certificate from the country of residence, not older than 6 months, with an authorized translation if not in English or a Nordic language
Medical-expense insurance confirmation, valid for at least six months from registration of legal domicile in Iceland, with a minimum coverage of ISK 2,000,000
Documents demonstrating secure financial support for the period of residence
Confirmed copy of the original birth certificate of the applicant's adult child residing in Iceland, with legal authentication if issued abroad
Authorized translation of the birth certificate if not in English or a Nordic language
Payment receipt for the application fee
Completed and signed application form (D-106/D-206)
Application for work permit and employment contract (if applicable)
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, ensuring they meet translation and authentication criteria.
Pay the application fee of 110,000 ISK via bank transfer and obtain a payment receipt.

Submit the completed and signed paper application form (D-106/D-206) along with all supporting documents, either by mail or in person at the Directorate of Immigration's reception or district commissioner's offices.

The Directorate of Immigration will process the application and may request additional information or documents. Applicants who require a visa to travel to Iceland must be outside Iceland during the application processing, while non-visa-exempt applicants may stay in Iceland if their presence remains legal.

Upon approval, the applicant must attend a photo session for the residence permit card, submit a notification of their place of residence, and undergo a medical examination within two weeks of arrival in Iceland, if applicable.

After fulfilling these conditions, the residence permit is issued, and the residence permit card will be available for collection approximately five days after the photo session. A national ID number (kennitala) will also be assigned.

visas.name: Work Permit for Expert Knowledge
visas.description: This permit is designed for non-EEA/EFTA/Faroese foreign experts with specialized knowledge and skills that are essential to an Icelandic company and cannot be found locally. It allows the individual to work for a specific employer in Iceland.
visas.target_applicant: Foreign experts from outside the EEA, EFTA, or Faroe Islands who possess expert knowledge, have a signed employment contract with an Icelandic employer, and whose skills are deemed essential and unavailable in the local or wider EEA/EFTA labor market.
visas.path_to_residency_description: A temporary work permit for expert knowledge can be renewed for up to two years at a time (and potentially up to four years in some cases) and can be used as the basis for applying for a permanent residence permit in Iceland after a qualifying period of legal residence.
visas.renewal_conditions: An application for extension must be submitted before the current permit expires, meet all the initial temporary work permit requirements, and the employer must have paid withholding tax and social security contributions for the individual's work.
visas.tax_implications: Foreign experts may be eligible for a discounted tax rate, where only 75% of their income earned in Iceland is subject to tax for the first three years of employment, provided certain conditions are met and an application is submitted within three months of starting work.
benefits: Permission to work and reside in Iceland for a specific employer.
Potential for a discounted tax rate, where only 75% of income is taxed for the first three years of work.
The permit is renewable and can lead to permanent residency.
Possibility of expedited application processing for the work and residence permit.
Family members may be allowed to join through family reunification work permits.
required_documents: Original application form for a temporary work permit for expert knowledge, fully completed and signed by both applicant and employer.
Employment contract between the applicant and the employer, including job title, description, and pension fund contributions, with terms similar to other experts in the sector.
Opinion of the relevant Icelandic trade union confirming employment terms conform to collective agreements (unless the union is Efling, in which case the Directorate of Labour obtains it).
Certified copy of diploma(s) in Icelandic or English, or evidence of extensive experience (generally at least seven years of relevant work experience is required to match a university degree).
Information regarding the employer's attempts to hire an Icelandic, EEA, EFTA, or Faroese national before hiring the foreign expert.
Justification from the employer regarding the need for the foreign national's expertise.
Passport copy (valid for the full permit duration).
Passport-sized photo (35mm x 45mm).
Original criminal record certificate (no older than 6 months) along with a translation.
Proof of health insurance valid for at least six months.
application_process_steps: The employer conducts a labor market test, demonstrating that the position cannot be filled by local or EEA/EFTA candidates, and prepares a job offer and employment contract.
The employer and applicant complete and sign the work permit application form and gather all required supporting documents.

The employer submits the work permit application to the Directorate of Immigration, which then forwards it to the Directorate of Labour for processing. (Work permit application fee is approximately ISK 20,000).
Once the work permit is granted by the Directorate of Labour, the applicant applies for a residence permit with the Directorate of Immigration.
The applicant pays the residence permit application fee (currently ISK 80,000).
Upon approval of both permits, the applicant can enter Iceland and must register legal domicile and submit biometrics.
Eligible foreign experts may apply for a tax discount through the Icelandic Centre for Research within three months of commencing work in Iceland.

visas.name: Work Permit due to Shortage of Labour
visas.description: This work permit is for non-EEA/EFTA nationals seeking employment in Iceland for specific jobs where no suitable candidates can be found within the Icelandic labor market or other EEA/EFTA member states. It is intended to address temporary fluctuations and shortages in the Icelandic labor market.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals from outside the EEA, EFTA, or Faroe Islands who have secured a job offer from an Icelandic employer for a position where a domestic or EEA/EFTA worker cannot be found.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After living in Iceland continuously for four years with a valid residence permit, individuals may apply for a permanent residence permit, provided certain conditions are met.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit can be renewed for up to two years, provided the applicant continues to meet the original conditions, including working for the same employer and in the same role (unless a change has been approved). An application for extension must be submitted to the Directorate of Immigration four weeks before the expiry of the previous permit.
visas.tax_implications: Standard resident tax rules apply. The employer is responsible for paying taxes and insurance premiums for the foreign worker.
benefits: Allows legal employment in Iceland for a specific job and employer.
Initial permit valid for up to one year, renewable for up to two years.
Includes the right to family reunification for spouses, children, and parents over 67 years of age.
Provides a pathway to permanent residency after four years of continuous residence.
If employment is dissolved, permit holders can apply for a 6-month residence permit to seek a new job.
required_documents: Original application for a temporary work permit due to a shortage of staff.
Employment contract, signed by both employee and employer, including wage figures or reference to relevant collective agreement.
Opinion of the relevant trade union (unless the union is Efling, in which case the Directorate of Labour obtains it).
Information and justification from the employer regarding attempts to hire within Iceland, the EEA, EFTA, or Faroe Islands (labor market test).
Justification for the necessity of hiring a foreign national from outside EEA/EFTA.
Valid passport.
Passport-sized photographs (35x45 mm).
Proof of health insurance.
Original criminal record along with a translation.
Company records (e.g., business registration certificate, tax compliance).
Certified copies of educational and professional qualifications (if applicable).
Instructions and checklists from the Directorate of Labour (to be followed).
Signatures of both applicant and employer on the application and contract.
application_process_steps: The employer defines the role and ensures salary and working conditions meet Icelandic collective agreements.
The employer coordinates with the Directorate of Labour, demonstrating that the position cannot be filled by domestic or EEA/EFTA workers (may involve advertising the role).
The employer and employee gather all required documentation, including the employment contract and trade union opinion.
The employer submits the application for a work permit along with the application for a residence permit to the Directorate of Immigration.
The Directorate of Immigration reviews the residence permit application and forwards the work permit application to the Directorate of Labour for processing.
Upon approval, the work permit is issued to both the individual and the employer. The employee may not start working before both the work and residence permits are granted.

visas.name: Temporary Work Permit for Seasonal Work
visas.description: This visa is for non-EEA/EFTA nationals seeking temporary employment in Iceland for seasonal work. It allows individuals to work in specific sectors, typically for short durations, to meet seasonal labor demands in industries like agriculture, fish processing, and tourism.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a non-EEA/EFTA national who has secured a confirmed job offer from an Icelandic employer for temporary seasonal work.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This permit generally does not count toward permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: An application for an extension must meet all the requirements of the temporary work permit, and the employer must have paid withholding tax and social security contributions for the work of the individual. Applications must be submitted at least one month before the current permit expires.
benefits: Opportunity to work legally in Iceland for a defined seasonal period.
Helps fill labor needs in key seasonal industries like tourism, agriculture, and fish processing.
Provides a pathway for temporary legal stay in Iceland for employment.
required_documents: Completed Visa Application Form from the Icelandic Directorate of Immigration website
Valid Passport (valid for at least three months beyond the intended stay, with at least two blank pages)
Two recent color passport photos meeting Schengen standards

Legally compliant Employment Contract signed by both the applicant and the Icelandic employer, including job title, description, pension fund contributions, and terms conforming to Icelandic collective agreements
Proof of Visa Fee Payment
Health Insurance policy valid in Iceland
Criminal Record Certificate (police clearance)
Proof of Qualifications (if applicable, certified copy in Icelandic or English, or evidence of extensive relevant experience)
Proof of Accommodation in Iceland
Documentation of the employer's attempts to recruit Icelandic, EEA, EFTA, or Faroese nationals before hiring the applicant
Confirmation from the employer to pay for the applicant's return travel if the contract is cut short due to reasons beyond their control or if they become disabled due to illness or accident
Opinion of the relevant trade union regarding the employment contract (in many cases)
application_process_steps: The employer finds a suitable non-EEA/EFTA candidate for a seasonal job.
The employer and the prospective employee sign a legally compliant employment contract.
The employer submits the application for a work permit, along with the application for a residence permit, to the Directorate of Immigration.
The Directorate of Immigration reviews the residence permit application; if conditions are met, it forwards the work permit application to the Directorate of Labour.
The Directorate of Labour processes and issues the work permit.
The employee may not commence work until the work permit has been granted.

visas.name: Work Permit for Athletes
visas.description: This permit allows non-EEA/EFTA athletes to work and reside in Iceland for a specific sports club. It is granted for playing or training a certain sport under an employment contract with an affiliated club.
visas.target_applicant: Professional athletes from outside the EEA/EFTA/Faroe Islands who have a confirmed employment contract with a sports club that is part of the Icelandic Olympic and Sports Association.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holders of this permit can work towards permanent residency in approximately 4 years, subject to meeting residence and other conditions.
visas.renewal_conditions: Same conditions as the initial application must be fulfilled. The sports club must have paid taxes and insurance premiums for the foreigner and other licensees. Application for extension must be submitted at least four weeks before the previous permit expires.
benefits: Permission to work legally in Iceland for a specific sports club.
Initial validity of up to two years, with possibilities for renewal.
A potential path to permanent residency after four years.
Ability to be present in Iceland while the application is processed, provided their stay is legal.
required_documents: Original application form for a temporary work permit for athletes.
Employment contract made between the individual and the sports club, signed by both parties.
Information about the planned work, proposed employment period (generally the coming season or competition season), pension funds payable, and pay conditions.
Confirmation that the employer pays for the repatriation of the individual after the end of the employment period in certain cases.
Valid passport (not older than 10 years and valid for at least three months after stay).
Passport-sized photo (35 x 45 mm).
Valid health insurance.
Original criminal record (background check) along with a translation.
Payment receipt for the processing fee.
application_process_steps: Secure an employment contract with an Icelandic sports club affiliated with the Icelandic Olympic and Sports Association.
Gather all required documents, including the original application and employment contract.
Pay the processing fee via bank transfer and obtain a payment receipt.
Submit the original application and all supporting documents to the Directorate of Immigration (Útlendingastofnun) via mail or drop-off.
The Directorate of Immigration assesses residence permit eligibility and forwards the work permit application to the Directorate of Labour.
The Directorate of Labour reviews the application and issues the work permit if all conditions are met.

visas.name: Work Permit for Researchers and Academic Staff
visas.description: This program is for non-EEA/EFTA researchers, academic staff, and specialists who have secured employment or an institutional invitation in Iceland for a period exceeding 90 days. It falls under the general category of 'Residence permit based on work' or 'work requiring expert knowledge'.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are non-EEA/EFTA citizens hired by Icelandic universities or research institutions, including guest researchers, lecturers, postdocs, and PhD students, who possess expert knowledge relevant to an Icelandic employer.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Four years of continuous legal residence in Iceland on a qualifying permit (such as this one) can lead to permanent residency. Applicants must also demonstrate Icelandic language proficiency, financial self-sufficiency, and a clean criminal record.
visas.renewal_conditions: Permits are renewed in accordance with an extended employment contract, provided there are no issues with wages or taxes. Renewal applications must be submitted at least one month before the current permit expires.
visas.tax_implications: Foreign experts may be eligible for a discounted tax rate.
benefits: Allows for long-term legal residency and employment in Iceland.
Provides a path to permanent residency after four years of continuous legal residence on a qualifying permit.
Dependants (spouses and children) are allowed to join the applicant.
May qualify for a discounted tax rate for foreign experts.
Initial permits are typically valid for one to two years and are renewable.
required_documents: Valid passport
Completed work permit application form, signed by applicant and employer
Employment contract with an Icelandic institution, including job title, description, and pension fund contributions
Certified copy of diploma(s) or evidence of expert knowledge and experience
Opinion from a relevant labour union confirming employment terms conform to Icelandic collective agreements (not required for cooperation agreements)
Documentation of secure means of support (e.g., tax returns or employment income)
Health insurance valid in Iceland for at least six months with minimum coverage of ISK 2,000,000
Passport-sized photo
Original criminal record certificate with a certified English translation
Cooperation agreement between domestic and foreign employer (for specialist teaching, academic or scientific workers under a contract)
Payment receipt for the application fee
application_process_steps: Secure an employment or cooperation contract with an Icelandic academic or research institution.
Complete the residence and work permit application form, ensuring both the applicant and employer sign it.
Obtain a union's opinion if applicable, verifying that the employment terms meet Icelandic collective agreements.
Gather all necessary supporting documents, including passport, diplomas, criminal record, and health insurance.
Pay the application fee via bank transfer and include the payment receipt with the application.
Submit the complete application package to the Directorate of Immigration (Útlendingastofnun) in paper form.

visas.name: Residence Permit for the Self-Employed
visas.description: This permit is designed for non-EEA/EFTA nationals who intend to establish and operate a genuine and viable business in Iceland, or manage an existing Icelandic company where their physical presence is deemed necessary and adds economic value to the country. It grants legal residency and the right to work within their self-employed business.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EEA/EFTA nationals who plan to actively run a legitimate business in Iceland, can demonstrate its economic benefit, and can financially support themselves through its operations.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Lawful continuous residence on a qualifying permit can lead to permanent residency after generally four continuous years. Applicants must demonstrate Icelandic language proficiency, financial self-sufficiency, and a clean criminal record.
visas.renewal_conditions: The business must remain genuine and active, and the applicant must continue to meet all residence conditions.
visas.tax_implications: Once tax residency is established (typically after 183 days of stay), standard resident tax rules apply. Self-employed individuals must register with the tax authority and pay income tax on their earnings. VAT registration is compulsory if the annual turnover exceeds ISK 2,000,000.
benefits: Legal residency in Iceland.
Right to operate and work within their own self-employed business.
Potential path to permanent residency.
Ability to bring dependants via family reunification.
required_documents: Valid passport and a recent photograph meeting official format.
Business plan and evidence that the business is genuine and viable.
Proof of means of support from the self-employed activity (e.g., annual financial statements, bank records).
Proof of housing in Iceland.
Health insurance certificate with a minimum coverage of ISK 2,000,000, valid in Iceland for at least six months from legal domicile registration.
Criminal record certificate.
Completed application form.
Registration as a self-employed person with Skatturinn (Icelandic tax authority).
application_process_steps: Confirm the self-employed activity is genuine, viable, and capable of providing sufficient financial support.
Gather all required documents, including a detailed business plan, proof of income, valid passport, housing arrangements, and health insurance.

Submit the completed application form, along with all supporting documents and the payment receipt for the application fee, to the Directorate of Immigration (paper applications require bank transfer payment).
Upon permit approval and arrival in Iceland, undergo a medical examination, report your place of residence, and appear for photography at the Directorate of Immigration within specified timeframes.
Maintain the genuine and active operation of the business and apply for renewal of the permit as required.

visas.name: Residence Permit for Financially Independent Persons
visas.description: Iceland does not offer a dedicated 'Residence Permit for Financially Independent Persons' in the traditional sense, where passive income alone is sufficient. Instead, individuals who do not qualify for other residence permits (e.g., work, study, family reunification) may apply for a 'Residence permit on grounds of legitimate and special purpose.' This permit is granted only in exceptional instances and requires applicants to demonstrate secure means of financial support and a 'legitimate and special purpose' for their stay in Iceland, which extends beyond mere financial independence.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals aged 18 or older who have a 'legitimate and special purpose' for residing in Iceland, do not meet the criteria for other residence permits, and can independently and securely support themselves financially for the duration of their stay.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Generally, a foreign national must have resided in Iceland on a qualifying residence permit continuously for four years to be eligible for a permanent residence permit.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet the requirements for secure means of support and the legitimate and special purpose for which the permit was originally granted.
benefits: Ability to reside in Iceland for a specific, legitimate purpose.
Potential path to permanent residency after four years of continuous legal residence on a qualifying permit.
Allows for family reunification with appropriate financial demonstration.
Access to Icelandic healthcare system upon registration of legal domicile and medical examination (if applicable).
required_documents: Valid passport (valid at least 90 days beyond permit validity, copy of personal information and signature page).
Recent passport photo (35x45 mm).
Proof of secure means of support (e.g., bank-account balances, tax returns – cash not accepted).
Statement describing the legitimate and special purpose of stay in Iceland.
Supporting documentation for the stated purpose of stay.
Health insurance valid in Iceland for at least six months with minimum 2,000,000 ISK coverage.
Criminal record certificate (not older than 12 months, from country of residence, issued by highest competent authority; translations required if not in English or Nordic language).
Proof of housing in Iceland.
Payment receipt for the application fee.
application_process_steps: Pay the application processing fee by bank transfer.
Submit the application form (on paper), along with the payment receipt and all required supporting documents, by mail or in person to the Directorate of Immigration.
Await processing and decision from the Directorate of Immigration (applicants needing a visa may not be in Iceland during processing).
If approved, attend a photo appointment for the residence permit card, submit a notification of residence, and undergo a medical examination (if applicable) within 90 days.
Receive the residence permit card and a personal identification number (kennitala).

Citizenship by Descent.desc: A child acquires Icelandic citizenship at birth if their mother is an Icelandic citizen, or if their father is an Icelandic citizen and married to the mother. This applies regardless of the child's birthplace. Children born abroad to an unmarried Icelandic father can acquire citizenship by registration before age 18. Since July 1, 2018, a child born to at least one Icelandic parent automatically acquires citizenship at birth, regardless of parents' marital status or where the birth occurred.

Naturalization.desc: The main path requires foreign nationals to have lived legally and continuously in Iceland for at least 7 years. Applicants must be 18 years or older, demonstrate knowledge of Icelandic (pass an Icelandic language test), prove financial stability and self-sufficiency, have no criminal record, and be of good character. Shorter residence periods apply for Nordic citizens (3 or 4 years), spouses of Icelandic nationals (3 or 4 years), registered cohabitants (5 years), and children of Icelandic citizens (2 years).

Birthright.desc: Iceland does not generally grant automatic citizenship by birth (jus soli) to children born on Icelandic soil to foreign parents. However, a child born in Iceland to stateless or unknown parents will become an Icelandic citizen. An exception also applies to children who are stateless at birth, have lived in Iceland continuously since birth, and resided in the country for at least 3 years at the time of notification before the age of 21.

Spouse and Family.desc: A foreigner married to an Icelandic citizen can apply for citizenship after 3 or 4 years of continuous residence in Iceland since the marriage, provided the Icelandic spouse has been a citizen for at least 5 years. For those cohabiting with an Icelandic citizen, citizenship can be obtained after at least 5 years of cohabitation registration, with the Icelandic partner also being a citizen for at least 5 years. Children born to one Icelandic and one foreign parent may acquire citizenship based on specific rules at the time of their birth, typically if the Icelandic parent held citizenship at that time.

tax_advice:
- **Personal Income Tax (PIT):** For 2026, taxable employment income is subject to progressive rates. These range from 31.49% on the first ISK 5,977,464 (ISK 498,122 per month), to 37.99% on income between ISK 5,977,465 and ISK 16,781,400 (ISK 498,123 to 1,398,450 per month), and 46.29% on income exceeding ISK 16,781,400 (ISK 1,398,451 per month). These rates include an average municipal income tax of 14.94%, which can vary slightly by municipality.
- **Personal Tax Credit:** For tax year 2026, the personal tax credit is ISK 869,898 annually (ISK 72,492 per month) deducted from calculated taxes for those with unlimited tax liability.
- **Capital Income Tax:** The tax rate on an individual's capital income is 22%. This applies to interest income exceeding ISK 300,000 per year. Rental income is also taxed at 22%, but only 25% of the rental income is liable to tax.
- **Payroll Tax (Social Security):** Employers are obligated to pay a payroll tax (social security tax) on employee remuneration, which is 6.35% for 2026.
- **Tax Residence:** Residents are generally taxed on their worldwide income, while non-residents are taxed on income derived from Icelandic sources. Residency for tax purposes is typically established by being domiciled in Iceland or staying for over 183 days in any 12-month period.
local_tips:
- **Cost of Living:** Iceland is one of the most expensive countries globally. For a single person in Reykjavik, estimated monthly costs (including rent) are around $3205 (ISK 556,439), with rent for a one-bedroom apartment in the city center typically ranging from 260,000–350,000 ISK per month in 2026.
- **Language:** While most Icelanders speak excellent English, learning Icelandic is highly recommended for deeper integration into society and the workplace. The language can be challenging to learn.
- **Safety:** Iceland consistently ranks as one of the safest countries in the world with a very low crime rate. Petty crime, such as pickpocketing, can occur in tourist areas, so basic precautions are advised. The main safety concerns are often related to rapidly changing weather conditions and natural phenomena.
- **Registration:** Upon moving to Iceland, expats need to register with Registers Iceland (Þjóðskrá) to obtain a kennitala (national ID number), which is essential for accessing healthcare, opening bank accounts, and employment. Residence permits are required for most non-EEA citizens, with financial self-sufficiency requirements updated in May 2026 to ISK 259,951 per month for an adult.
- **Healthcare:** After legally residing in Iceland for six months, you become part of the public health insurance system, which is tax-funded and provides affordable care. Many residents also opt for private health insurance to supplement coverage.
